digests.headline: No football yet, but Chelsea just bought a centre-back and stole Villa's set-piece brain
digests.yesterday: No match, but a properly busy day at the club. Maxence Lacroix completed his medical in London, with Romano reporting the £52m deal wraps this week — and the fan threads were quick to note he's Chelsea's first paid signing aged 26 or over since summer 2022, which tells you something about the profile shift. The quieter coup might be Austin MacPhee: Chelsea triggered the release clause for Aston Villa's set-piece coach, the man behind the best set-piece attack in Europe's top five leagues in 2023–24. And the Kerim Alajbegović pursuit rumbles on — Leverkusen want big money, Romano insists Chelsea won't go near £34m, so expect a few more days of briefing wars.
digests.today: Nothing on — no Chelsea match, no Premier League, and the table below is alphabetical because nobody has kicked a ball yet (that's why Bournemouth are 'top' and Chelsea '6th'). Pre-season is on the way and the subreddit is already counting down. If you need live football today, Wafcon 2026 is about to start; otherwise this is a guilt-free night off.

wider.title: Chelsea in talks for Aston Villa set-piece guru MacPhee
wider.hook: The numbers on why this hire matters: under MacPhee, Villa out-scored every side in Europe's top five leagues from set pieces in 2023–24. Chelsea just bought that edge.

wider.title: [Romano] Maxence Lacroix completed his medical in London as new Chelsea player
wider.hook: The £52m deal is effectively done — and the comments are where the real debate is: is this the experienced head the back line has been missing, or a squeeze on Neto and Gittens?

wider.title: Como become the first club to ban headers in their youth academy
wider.hook: Raphaël Varane's brain-injury advocacy just became actual club policy. The thread is a genuinely good argument about where the game goes from here.
